title: Invariant coverage tax: totality versus proportionality

completion_criteria.text: Map the enforcement chain end to end and write it down: registry, coverage entry, checker modes, CI wiring, and exactly where the seventeen-row obligation is generated
Measure the real cost rather than assert it: what a full coverage entry actually costs on a low-risk change, and how that scales as the registry grows past seventeen ids
Settle against M1 and M2 as ratified: does proportional coverage necessarily reintroduce the self-selected allowlist M2 forbids, or is there a form that does not
Choose one resolution on robustness first then simplicity, record the decision, and name explicitly what it gives up
Implement it with red-before/green-after receipts and its own coverage entry, then ship one PR via pr-create

spine.active_goal: Decide whether the total-coverage obligation stays as ratified or becomes a machine-proved inert predicate, then ship that choice.
spine.next_step: START c2 in a FRESH session. Measure the cost rather than estimate it: time and token cost of one full seventeen-row entry on a low-risk change, and how it scales at 30 ids. Only then ratify or reject the inert-predicate shape in c4. Do NOT skip c2 into implementation - the recommendation currently rests on an estimate, and c2 is what would falsify it.
spine.last_session: Opened the thread, mapped the enforcement chain (c1 done), and drafted c3's answer: a registry-declared, CI-evaluated inert predicate - never a per-change declaration.

open_risks.text: The inert predicate must belong to the INVARIANT in registry.json, never to the change — a per-change declaration is the self-selected allowlist the ratified spec forbids, whatever it is named

The polarity must stay inert, so an unenumerated path FALSIFIES the basis and forces prose — flip it to positive matching and the gate stops halting on the unclassifiable, which is M2 evaded rather than satisfied
An inert basis cannot be evaluated when no base resolves and must then fail loudly — that is a live behavior change from what 0264 shipped for push mode, so it needs a test rather than an argument
The checker is itself a gate, so M2, M3 and M6 apply to any change to it — a halt-on-unclassifiable test, a red-on-parent acceptance test, and a deployed-artifact check are all owed
An over-broad inert_when glob is the primary failure mode, and this is a solo repo where the author is the reviewer — do not rely on PR review to catch a glob that is too wide

out_of_scope: Moving the verdict into the PR body - pr-create's flag set is closed and its values cap at 200 characters, which is why M1 puts the verdict in a committed artifact
Any resolution needing a second reviewer, a bot account, or org-level infrastructure - this is a solo owner-held repo
